text:
Obama 
Chelsea Manning
Army intelligence analyst convicted of leaking hundreds of thousands of classified military and diplomatic documents to WikiLeaks. Obama commuted the remaining 28 years of a 35-year sentence so Manning would be released after roughly seven years. Republicans including Sen. John McCain, Rep. Mac Thornberry, and House Speaker Paul Ryan called it outrageous, and an act that treated “espionage” lightly and put troops at risk. Critics labeled Manning a traitor; supporters called the original sentence excessive. The commutation stood; 

https://t.co/q351UAZrzP

Oscar López Rivera
Member of the FALN, a Puerto Rican nationalist group that claimed responsibility for dozens of bombings in U.S. cities in the 1970s–80s. He was serving a long sentence for seditious conspiracy and related charges (not a specific bombing conviction). Obama commuted it so he would be released after 36 years. Victims’ families (including an op-ed by the son of a Fraunces Tavern bombing victim), columnists, and some law-enforcement voices condemned the decision and described López Rivera as a terrorist. Supporters called him a political prisoner. Clinton had previously offered him conditional clemency, which he declined. Again, the grant was public and was not reversed. 

https://t.co/b31RV1PJsf
High profile pardons
James Cartwright — retired Marine general, pleaded guilty to lying to the FBI in a leak probe related to Stuxnet/Iran. Pardon, not a commutation from a long sentence.
 pardons such as Willie McCovey (tax evasion) and Ian Schrager (Studio 54 tax case).
Biden
Hunter Biden (pardon, December 1, 2024)
Son of the president. Convicted on federal gun and tax charges; about to be sentenced. Biden issued a broad pardon covering offenses from January 1, 2014 through December 1, 2024 — after repeatedly saying he would not pardon him.

Leonard Peltier (commutation, last hours of the presidency)
Native American activist convicted of the 1975 murders of two FBI agents on the Pine Ridge Reservation. Life sentence commuted; he was released to home confinement after decades in prison. FBI families, law-enforcement groups, and many Republicans condemned it. Supporters had long called him a political prisoner. This is the closest Biden analogue to Obama’s Oscar López Rivera case. 

https://t.co/G7myA88Fwo

37 federal death-row inmates (commutations to life without parole, December 23, 2024)
Biden spared 37 of 40 people on federal death row. They were not let out. Every one had a murder conviction; one case also involved sexual abuse of the victim. Victims’ families, Trump, and many prosecutors called it a betrayal of justice. Trump later ordered harsher conditions and encouraged states to seek new capital charges. Biden left three on death row: Dylann Roof, Robert Bowers (Tree of Life synagogue), and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev (Boston Marathon). Two of the 37 even tried to reject the commutation so they could keep appealing.

Capitol and D.C. police who testified

It did not pardon the Texas sex case. Harris County still had the warrant. He later pled to the old state charge and got credit for time Biden’s DOJ already made him https://t.co/sIlLylFXCL your example is: Biden prosecuted a riot case, Trump undid the riot case, and a 2016 state sex charge that sat there the entire Biden presidency is still on him. That’s not “Trump let a child predator out.” That’s you mixing two different cases because one name is convenient.If we’re counting who actually cut time for people already convicted of sex trafficking and child porn, that’s Biden (Jin swap, Graham, Shine, death-row rape-murders taken off the needle). Trump’s Jan 6 pardon covered the federal riot/assault case. The 2016 online solicitation of a minor was a pending Texas state charge from years earlier. The pardon did not wipe that case. He later pled and got credit for time already served. That is not “Trump commuted a child-sex sentence.”
Jin is not a “wrongfully detained American.” He was a Chinese national sentenced to 8 years for possessing tens of thousands of child-porn images. Biden commuted that sentence so he could be swapped and deported to China instead of serving it here. Clemency for a child-porn convict is still clemency for a child-porn convict, swap or not.
Jackson staying in prison for life is exactly what the original post said. Commuting a death sentence for kidnapping, rape, and murder is still mercy for a rapist-murderer. Same with Avila-Torrez (raped and stabbed two little girls), Gabrion, Basham/Fulks, etc. They are not walking free. They were taken off death row.

If the standard is “did they cut time for people with sex crimes,” Biden did it in the late-term “nonviolent drug” batches too:Lairon Graham: pleaded to fentanyl conspiracy and four counts of sex trafficking by force/coercion. Judge called it one of the most heinous cases he’d seen. Biden cut 22 years to 12½.  
Valentino Shine Sr.: jury convicted him of running a sex-trafficking operation, beating and doping women, three of whom later overdosed. 30 years cut to about 18.

Those men get out years earlier because Biden labeled the cases “drug.”Obama’s record is the same pattern at scale: 1,715 commutations. He also put Oscar López Rivera back on the street — FALN leadership tied to a bombing campaign that killed and maimed civilians. Clinton had already offered him a deal; Obama finished the job.Nobody said every commutation dumps a rapist on the sidewalk the next morning. The point is simple: Obama and Biden repeatedly used clemency to shorten time for people whose records include rape, child porn, sex trafficking, and terrorism-linked violence, then sold it as “nonviolent second chances.” That’s the record. Taake doesn’t erase it.

text:
[The Most Important Question Is: “Who Are You?”]
— What Must Humans Complete After AI?

Recently in South Korea,

discussions have continued

over the possible integration
of the military academies
of the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

Those in favor

talk about

educational efficiency
and jointness.

Those opposed

talk about

the traditions
and identities

of each branch.

This debate

is not simply

about whether
the academies should be merged.

It raises

a deeper question.

“Who are we?”

──────────────────

AI

connects information rapidly

and expands

many of the capabilities
human beings possess.

As technology advances

and more people gain access
to similar tools,

a new set of questions

becomes increasingly important.

What distinguishes us?

Who am I?

What do we exist for?

These are

questions of identity.

──────────────────

A military

does not become strong

through weapons alone.

What do we exist

to protect?

A shared answer
to that question

creates

organizational cohesion

and standards
for action.

That is why

military identity

is not merely
a matter of tradition.

It is also

an important standard

that determines

what an organization
exists to protect

and how it should act.

──────────────────

This question

is not only
for the military.

What value

will a company
take responsibility for
to the end?

What kind of human beings

will a university
educate?

With what philosophy

will a nation
build its future?

And

why do

human beings exist?

──────────────────

AI

can provide

countless answers.

“Who am I?”

“Why do we exist?”

AI may also

offer answers
to these questions.

But

choosing which answer

will become
your own,

living that answer,

and taking responsibility
for that choice

belong to
human beings.

Perhaps identity

is the continuing answer

to the questions:

Who am I?

And

what do I exist for?

──────────────────

As technology advances,

questions of identity

may become
even more important.

What matters

is not choosing

between technology
and identity.

What will we use

technology for?

In what direction

will we use it?

Those standards

become increasingly important.

Technology

can expand
our capabilities.

But

human beings
must choose

the direction

in which those capabilities
will be used.

──────────────────

1030 Young Stars,

after AI,

as more people gain access

to similar technologies,

there are questions

that become
even more important.

Who am I?

What do I exist for?

AI

can provide

countless answers.

But

choosing an answer,

living it,

and taking responsibility
for it

belong to
human beings.

Who are you?

Your answer
to that question

shapes
your direction.

— Captain Kang Sangbo
Civilization Designer
Commander-in-Chief,
Gaegeunsang United Grand Fleet

text:
The US has opened a financial front against Iran, aimed at the payment channels its naval blockade cannot reach.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the department has launched Operation Economic Outcast to cut off all financial lifelines to the Iranian regime and its enablers, with awards offered for actionable tips from anywhere in the world.

Bessent said the US is "no longer managing the Iranian threat. We are ending it."

The blockade was reinstated on July 14. CENTCOM says 103 commercial vessels have been redirected since it resumed.

US forces destroyed two Iranian small boats on Monday after the IRGC tried to seize a Navy drone in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials told Axios.

Analysts expecting Tehran to absorb this round point to decades of experience with US restrictions and to oil sales settled in yuan with China.

The rial has fallen sharply since the blockade resumed, which analysts read as evidence of lost oil revenue and costlier imports. Iran has no workaround for the blockade itself.

text:
I retired at 20 because I put forth the best effort I could. I took every job offered, had 4.0 marks. 
I was missing a single qualification (Enlisted Surface Warfare Specialist) in the Navy, not because I didn't try for it. Because my Department Head & Division Officer at the time refused permission for me to complete the required training while I was on board the USS Theodore Roosevelt!! 

I was given no recourse it went all the way up the chain to the ships CO, since it wasn't endorsed positively by immediate chain he didn't approve it. 

Back then in the 1980s if you were an E-6 trying for E-7 and had served on a ship in the Navy and then left without that pin you didn't get selected for E7.
I had no choice. I was not selected for E-7 and therefore forced into mandatory retirement as an E6 at 20 years! A few days before my actual retirement I was informed that I could come back as an E-7  because I had finally after been selected! 🙄

By then it just didn't feel worth the effort. I had moved & resettled. It literally didn't feel like a reward for service as much as a token gift to try and keep me around.
